title: I'm not feeling well
goal: Name parts of the body, explain what's wrong at a clinic or pharmacy, and use possessive forms for things that belong to you.
bekal: say what hurts with *'indii alam fii...*

dialogs.title: حِوَار — فِي الْعِيَادَةِ
dialogs.intro: Budi goes to the campus clinic because he has had a fever for two days.

lines.speaker: اَلطَّبِيبَة:
lines.id: Come in, have a seat. What's wrong?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.id: I have a fever and a headache.
lines.literal: at-me heat and pain in head-my.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.baca: mundhu yaumain. wa halqii yu'limunii aiḍan.
lines.id: For two days. My throat hurts too.
lines.literal: since two-days. and throat-my hurts-me also.

lines.speaker: اَلطَّبِيبَة:
lines.baca: hal tas'ul? wa hal nimta jayyidan?
lines.id: Are you coughing? And are you sleeping well?
lines.literal: do you-cough? and do you-sleep well?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: نَعَمْ أَسْعُلُ قَلِيلًا، وَمَا نِمْتُ جَيِّدًا.
lines.baca: na'am as'ulu qaliilan, wa maa nimtu jayyidan.
lines.id: Yes, I'm coughing a little, and I didn't sleep well.
lines.literal: yes I-cough a-little, and not I-slept well.

lines.speaker: اَلطَّبِيبَة:
lines.text: لَا تَقْلَقْ. هٰذِهِ نَزْلَةُ بَرْدٍ بَسِيطَةٌ.
lines.baca: laa taqlaq. haadhihi nazlatu bardin basiiṭah.
lines.id: Don't worry. It's just a mild cold.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.id: Thank God. What should I take?

lines.speaker: اَلطَّبِيبَة:
lines.text: خُذْ هٰذَا الدَّوَاءَ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ فِي الْيَوْمِ.
lines.id: Take this medicine three times a day.
lines.literal: take this medicine three times in the-day.

lines.speaker: اَلطَّبِيبَة:
lines.text: بَعْدَ الْأَكْلِ. وَاشْرَبْ مَاءً كَثِيرًا وَاسْتَرِحْ.
lines.id: After meals. And drink plenty of water and rest.
lines.literal: after the-eating. and drink water much and rest.

notes: **مَاذَا بِكَ؟ is literally "what is with you?".** It's the standard doctor's question, and also what people say when you look unwell. To a woman: مَاذَا بِكِ؟ More casual: مَا لَكَ؟

**عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي... — the standard way to name a complaint.** "I have pain in ...". An equally common alternative: رَأْسِي يُؤْلِمُنِي ("my head hurts me") — here the body part is the subject, not you.

**Body parts that come in pairs are feminine.** يَد (hand), عَيْن (eye), رِجْل (leg, foot), أُذُن (ear) — all feminine even without ة. This continues the list of exceptions from unit 3, and the reason is simply that: Arabic treats paired body parts as feminine.
**مُنْذُ يَوْمَيْنِ — the dual after a preposition.** يَوْمَانِ becomes يَوْمَيْنِ because مُنْذُ comes before it. You saw this with صَدِيقَيْنِ in unit 13; the pattern is consistent.
**نِمْتُ, not نَامْتُ.** نَامَ is a hollow verb like كَانَ and زَارَ: the middle letter drops out as soon as the ending starts with a consonant. نَامَ → نِمْتُ, قَامَ → قُمْتُ, بَاعَ → بِعْتُ.
**أَمْ, not أَوْ.** Both mean "or", but أَمْ is used in **either-or questions**: قَبْلَ الْأَكْلِ أَمْ بَعْدَهُ؟ Outside questions you use أَوْ: شَايٌ أَوْ قَهْوَةٌ.

**سَلَامَتُكَ and أَلْفُ سَلَامَةٍ are get-well wishes.** The ones you'll hear most: سَلَامَتُكَ ("may you be well"), أَلْفُ سَلَامَةٍ ("a thousand wishes of safety"), شِفَاءً عَاجِلًا ("get well soon"). The reply: اَللهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ ("may God keep you safe too").

grammars.title: Saying what's wrong
after: أَشْعُرُ بِـ ("I feel") is always followed by بِ and a noun: أَشْعُرُ بِالْبَرْدِ (I feel cold), أَشْعُرُ بِالْجُوعِ (I feel hungry), أَشْعُرُ بِتَحَسُّنٍ (I feel better).

grammars.title: Parts of the body
after: Some of these traveled far beyond Arabic: قَلْب lives on in Turkish *kalp*, Urdu *qalb* and Malay *kalbu*, and وَجْه in Malay *wajah*.
To say "my", attach ـِي as usual: رَأْسِي, يَدِي, بَطْنِي. Note that رِجْل becomes رِجْلِي and عَيْن becomes عَيْنِي.

Meaning
rows: Do you have something for a headache?

blocks.title: Sentences to memorize whole before you travel
items: **عِنْدِي حَسَاسِيَّةٌ مِنْ...** — "I'm allergic to...". This sentence can save a life, and it's not one to build while you think.
**أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى طَبِيبٍ** — "I need a doctor". And **أَيْنَ أَقْرَبُ مُسْتَشْفًى؟** — "where's the nearest hospital?".
Also keep one sentence ready about any chronic condition you have, for example عِنْدِي مَرَضُ السُّكَّرِ ("I have diabetes") or عِنْدِي رَبْوٌ ("I have asthma").

sections.title: Asking after the sick and wishing them well

blocks.text: The last phrase is used far beyond illness: you say it to anyone who has just come back from a trip, just recovered, or just got through something difficult. The reply: اَللهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ.

items: I've had a fever for two days.

answers: عِنْدِي حَرَارَةٌ مُنْذُ يَوْمَيْنِ. — عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي رَأْسِي. — وَحَلْقِي يُؤْلِمُنِي أَيْضًا. — كَمْ مَرَّةً فِي الْيَوْمِ؟ — بَعْدَ الْأَكْلِ. — شِفَاءً عَاجِلًا.
عَيْنِي / عَيْنَيَّ — أُذُنِي — رِجْلِي — فَمِي — يَدِي
مُنْذُ مَتَى؟ — هَلْ تَسْعُلُ؟ — كَمْ مَرَّةً فِي الْيَوْمِ؟ — قَبْلَ الْأَكْلِ أَمْ بَعْدَهُ؟ — هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَسَاسِيَّةٌ؟

Example: مَاذَا بِكَ؟ — عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي بَطْنِي مُنْذُ أَمْسِ — مُنْذُ مَتَى؟ — مُنْذُ أَمْسِ، وَمَا نِمْتُ جَيِّدًا — خُذْ هٰذَا الدَّوَاءَ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْمِ وَاسْتَرِحْ — شُكْرًا يَا دُكْتُورَة! وَجَوَابُهَا: سَلَامَتُكَ
wave: Memorize three sentences from this unit word for word: the allergy, needing a doctor, and the nearest hospital. These are not sentences to go hunting for when you need them.
